newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine oil dealers seek hike in margins.
newsitem.headline: Philippine oil dealers seek hike in margins.

text.p: Some 3,000 Philippine petroleum dealers are asking for an average six centavo per litre increase in their margins, the Federation of Petroleum Dealers of the Philippines said (FPDP) on Tuesday.

"We hope that next time the oil companies raise pump prices, they will consider a six centavo additional margin for dealers to cover the added operational cost of labor," FPDP president Perlita Villafuerte told Reuters by phone.
The federation represents the dealers associations of the country's three oil refiners.
Petron Corp, Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp and Caltex (Philippines) Inc have an estimated total of 3,000 petroleum dealers nationwide.
Villafuerte said the dealers had last year sought the Energy Regulatory Board's permission for an average ten centavo per litre increase in margins of which only half was granted.
She said the dealers' application was overtaken by plans to deregulate the oil industry. Villafuerte said the six centavos will cover for the increase in rentals and wages last year.
Under full deregulation which started on February 8, the oil companies as well as the dealers may adjust prices without approval of the government.

"But we have pledged to stick to the suggested pump price of the oil companies. So, we are asking the oil firms to consider including our six centavo proposed increase next time they adjust prices," Villafuerte said.

At present, dealers have a 62 centavos per litre mark-up for gasoline products, 50 centavos for diesel and 48 centavos for kerosene, Villafuerte said. On the average, dealers' mark-up amount to 55 centavos per litre of petroleum products.
